newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Muoi slams graft as source of inequality.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Muoi slams graft as source of inequality.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party chief has rounded on corrupt officials and slammed graft as a growing source of social inequality and waste, the Nhan Dan official daily said on Saturday.
"This problem is a major concern for the whole of society," party Secretary General Do Muoi was quoted as saying in a closing speech to a meeting of the party's Central Committee.
"Corruption and wastefulness of public property is increasing, causing losses in lives and material losses and exacerbating social inequality," he said.

Muoi told the committee's 170 members that it was their job to set a good example in fighting against the scourge of corruption and said they should be held responsible for graft, waste and bureaucracy in their official departments.
The State Inspectorate said earlier this week that it would consider a new anti-corruption bill which prescribes the death penalty for officials who rake off state funds.

A senior officer of the inspectorate said it had been suggested that any state or military official found guilty of siphoning off 300 million dong ($27,000) or more should be executed by firing squad or at least be imprisoned for life.

The new bill would be the country's first legal document aimed at curbing graft, which has been fed in recent years by an environment of reform-led prosperity growth and continued state control in most sectors of the economy.
Earlier this year, a Hong Kong-based consultancy survey named China, Indonesia and Vietnam as Asia's most graft-ridden nations.
The official Hanoi Moi daily said on Monday that 4,900 corruption cases causing economic losses of over $145 million were uncovered in the first nine months of this year alone.
The domestic press has given unprecedented coverage to several high-profile corruption scandal in recent months.
On Saturday, the Lao Dong newspaper reported the case of four people who were imprisoned for a total of 53 years for siphoning off the equivalent of $125,500 from a social insurance fund.
